transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, thank you so much for fitting me in. I really appreciate it. 

Um, I guess I'm here because... well, my sleep has just been a little off lately. I know everyone gets stressed with their jobs, and I don't want to make a big deal out of it, but I barely sleep in any useful way anymore. I'll just lie awake at night replaying client financial models in my head, trying to make sure everything is perfect. And then, if I do drift off, I end up waking up at 3 or 4 in the morning with my stomach all tight. 

I still go to the office and get everything done, of course, but I just go to work feeling like I never actually rested. I hope I'm explaining that right... is that the sort of thing I should be bringing up here?
When you're lying awake at night, is it mainly because you're having trouble falling asleep, or is it more that you're feeling anxious and can't quiet your mind?

Um, I suppose it's mostly my mind just... not shutting off. I hope I'm not making it sound like I'm completely falling apart, because I really am still keeping up with everything at the firm. But like I was saying, it just feels like I don't get any truly useful sleep anymore. 

I'll be physically exhausted, but I just lie there and my brain won't stop replaying those client models over and over. And then, if I finally do manage to drop off, that's when I get that 3 or 4 AM wake-up where my stomach is all in knots. So by the time I actually go to work, I just feel like I never really went to bed. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of information.
Do you find that your anxiety or worry continues even when there isn’t a specific work-related problem or deadline that you’re dealing with?

Um, well... I guess I wouldn't say I'm always worried. I mean, everyone has some level of stress, right? And I really try to leave work at work, so to speak. 

I suppose there are times when things are quiet at the firm and I still feel a little... on edge, maybe? But it's nothing I can't handle. I definitely don't want to give the impression that I'm just sitting around worrying about nothing all the time. I try to stay positive and keep busy. 

Is that normal? I mean, to sometimes just feel a bit tense even when there isn't a big deadline? I hope I'm not overcomplicating things.
Do you find yourself worrying about a variety of different things, even when there isn't a clear reason or specific problem to focus on?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try not to be one of those people who just worries about everything under the sun, you know? I really do try to focus on the positives. 

I guess... well, sometimes my mind might wander a bit to things like, I don't know, if the house is organized or if I'm keeping up with my friends enough, but I wouldn't call it worrying exactly. It's more just... being responsible, I think? I definitely don't want you to think I'm just sitting around agonizing over every little thing in my life. I really do keep it together pretty well most of the time. 

Does that sound like the right track? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly.
Do you ever feel like you can't control the worrying, even when you try to stop thinking about work or other responsibilities?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I really wouldn't say it's out of control. I mean, I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just spiraling or anything like that. 

If I really need to, I can usually just... pull myself together, you know? I like to think I have a pretty good handle on things. I mean, sure, sometimes it takes a little effort to switch gears and put the firm out of my mind for the evening, but I wouldn't call it uncontrollable. I'm still very capable of managing myself and my responsibilities. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I just really don't want to give you the wrong idea about how I'm functioning. Am I making sense?
Do you find yourself feeling noticeably more anxious or worried than other people in similar situations, even about things that most might consider minor or routine?

Um, I don't really think so. I mean, I try to keep things in perspective. I definitely don't want to come across as overly dramatic or anything. 

I think I handle things pretty much the same way anyone else in my position would. Maybe I'm a little thorough, but I wouldn't say I'm noticeably more anxious than other people. I really try to be resilient and just deal with whatever comes up without making a fuss about it. 

I hope that's what you were asking? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture. I'm really trying to be helpful.
Do you find yourself feeling unusually tired or low on energy during the day, even after trying to rest?

Um, no, I wouldn't say unusually tired. I mean, I work full time at the firm, and that's naturally going to take a lot out of anyone, right? I try to keep my energy up as best I can. 

I definitely don't want to sound like I'm just dragging myself around all day or being lazy. I make sure I get my work done and keep up with everything I need to do. Sometimes I might feel a little drained by the late afternoon, but I think that's just normal for someone my age with a demanding job. I really try to push through it. 

Is that the kind of thing you're looking for? I just want to make sure I'm not making it sound worse than it is. I'm really trying to be accurate for you.
Do you often experience physical symptoms like the stomach tightness you mentioned even when you're not particularly stressed or anxious?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. I mean, the stomach tightness really only happens when things are getting a bit intense at work, like before a big presentation or something. 

I wouldn't say it just happens out of nowhere. I really try to keep myself in check, and I definitely don't want you to think my body is just reacting to nothing. I think it's a pretty normal response to a high-pressure environment, right? I mean, anyone would feel a little knot in their stomach when there's a lot on the line. 

I really hope I'm answering this right. I just want to be sure I'm giving you the information you need without making it sound like I'm falling apart or anything. Am I doing okay with these questions?
Do you ever find yourself getting anxious or worried specifically about not being able to sleep, even before you go to bed?

Um, no, not really. I mean, I try not to let myself get worked up about sleep. That seems like it would just make things worse, right? 

I really try to just have a normal nighttime routine and wind down like anyone else. I definitely don't want to sound like I'm obsessing over it or laying there panicking about not sleeping before I even get into bed. If I have a restless night here and there, I just figure it's part of being a busy professional. I try to just take it in stride.

I hope that makes sense? I'm really trying to give you the right idea of how I handle things. I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and not overcomplicating everything.
Do you often find yourself worrying about small or routine things, even when you know logically that they probably aren’t a big deal?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I worry about small things. I mean, I'm an analyst, so my job is literally about paying attention to details and managing risks. It's just part of how I'm wired to, you know, be thorough and prepared. 

I definitely don't want you to think I'm sitting around fretting over every little thing or making mountains out of molehills. I think I handle the day-to-day stuff pretty well, just like anyone else trying to keep their life organized. If I double-check something, it's just to be responsible, not because I'm irrationally worried about it. 

Is that what you mean? I just want to make sure I'm not giving you the impression that I'm overly anxious about normal, everyday things. I'm really trying to give you a clear picture of how I operate.
Have you noticed any days where you feel anxious or have physical symptoms like stomach tightness even when there isn’t any particular work pressure or external stressor happening?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. When there's no pressure, like on a quiet weekend, I'm usually just... fine. I really try to leave work at work and enjoy my downtime, you know? 

I wouldn't say I get that stomach tightness for absolutely no reason. That sounds like I'm just kind of... falling apart out of nowhere, and I promise I'm not doing that. I really try to keep a good handle on things. If I do feel a little tense on a day off, it's usually just because I'm mentally prepping for the week ahead or thinking through a client's portfolio, which is pretty standard for my field. But not just out of the blue. 

Does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm giving you accurate answers and being a good patient. I really don't want to give you the wrong impression about how I cope with things.
Do you often feel a strong need to be in control of everything in your life, to the point where it causes you distress if things aren’t going exactly as planned?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I need to control *everything*. I mean, I like things to be organized and for plans to go smoothly, but I think that's just being responsible, right? 

I definitely don't get distressed or upset if things change. I'm pretty adaptable. In my line of work, the markets are always shifting, so you have to be able to pivot. I really try to just go with the flow when things don't pan out exactly how I expected in my personal life, too. I don't want you to think I'm some sort of control freak who falls apart if a dinner reservation gets canceled or something. I try to be very easygoing about that kind of stuff.

I hope I'm answering this the right way? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need and not making it sound like I'm overly rigid or difficult to be around.
Do you often find yourself feeling anxious or worried about a number of different everyday things, even when you know there may not be a clear reason to be concerned about them?

Um, no, I wouldn't say I worry about a bunch of different things without a reason. Like I mentioned, if I'm thinking about something, it's usually tied to work or, you know, making sure my life is running smoothly. 

I definitely don't want to come across like a worrier who just sits around spinning her wheels over nothing. I try really hard to stay grounded and focus on what's actually in front of me. I mean, everyone has passing thoughts, right? But I don't let them take over or get anxious over everyday stuff that doesn't matter. I really try to just handle my business and keep moving forward. 

Is that helpful? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of examples and not sounding like I'm anxious all the time. I'm really trying to be helpful here.

Oh, um... no, not really. I mean, sleep is important, obviously, but I don't lay awake worrying about *not* sleeping. That sounds like it would just make it worse, right? 

If I'm awake, it's usually just because I'm naturally a little restless or maybe I had a late cup of coffee. I definitely don't have this, like, anxiety about the act of sleeping itself. I try to practice good sleep hygiene and just let my body rest when it's ready. I'm pretty sensible about it.

I wouldn't want you to think I'm making a mountain out of a molehill when it comes to bedtime. I really try to just keep things normal and manageable. Am I explaining that okay? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the right picture of how I handle things.

Um, no, not really. I mean, I think about the future, of course, because I have to plan for things—especially with my job, you're always looking ahead at projections and stuff. But I wouldn't call it worrying or being anxious about things for no reason. 

I try to be really rational about what's coming up. I don't sit around imagining worst-case scenarios or anything like that. I feel like that would just be a waste of energy, you know? I really try to stay positive and just deal with things as they come, rather than borrowing trouble. 

I definitely don't want to sound like a pessimist or someone who's always anticipating disaster. I really try to keep a good perspective on things. Does that make sense? I hope I'm giving you the right kind of answers... I just want to make sure I'm doing this right for you.

Um, no, I wouldn't say I feel restless or anxious just out of the blue like that. I mean, I like to stay busy, and sometimes if I have a little downtime, I might feel like I should be doing something productive, you know? But I wouldn't call it anxiety. 

I really try to keep a level head and not let myself get worked up over nothing. I think it's important to be able to just relax when you can, and I try to do that. I definitely wouldn't want you to think I'm just sitting around vibrating with nervous energy for no reason. I try to be very steady. 

Is that the kind of thing you're asking about? I just want to make sure I'm not misunderstanding the question and giving you useless information. I really want to be as helpful as I can.

Oh, um... no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, obviously I care about my family and my health and everything, but I don't really fret over them. 

I try to be pretty practical about my personal life. If a friend needs me, I'm there, and if I need to go to the doctor for a checkup, I go, but I don't sit around spinning my wheels worrying about what *could* go wrong. I think it's really important to just maintain good, stable relationships and not create unnecessary drama, you know? 

I definitely don't want to be one of those people who is always complaining or stressing out everyone around them. I really try to be a steady presence for the people in my life. I like to think I handle things pretty gracefully.

Um, no... not really. I mean, routine things are just... routine, right? I actually kind of prefer having a set way of doing things, it keeps the day organized. So, no, I definitely don't get worked up over little everyday errands or minor situations. 

I really try to just handle what needs to be handled without making a fuss. I'd hate to be the sort of person who gets overwhelmed by just... normal daily life. I like to think I'm pretty capable when it comes to all the day-to-day stuff, and I just push through it.

I really try to be easygoing about that sort of thing.

I feel like I'm not giving you very much to go on with all these questions about anxiety. I hope I'm not being difficult or unhelpful... I just really don't want to exaggerate anything or make myself sound like a nervous wreck when I'm really trying my best to just hold everything together. Is this okay? I'm trying to answer exactly what you're asking.
